classification.difficultyReason: Find perpendicular component lengths in congruent slant faces, then apply the cosine rule in the internal triangle.

spec.description: Unshaded tetrahedron with apex O above the equilateral base ABC, X on OC, hidden edges through B dashed, and the construction segments XA and XB solid.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CA=6 cm; OA=OB=OC=8 cm; X lies on OC; XA and XB are perpendicular to OC. Explicit vertices and projected viewing direction are recorded in the editable code.

answer.short:
$\angle AXB=65.28^\circ$.

Find $XA=XB$ from the perpendicular triangles, then use the cosine rule in $\triangle AXB$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle OCA$, use the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle OCA&=\frac{8^2+6^2-8^2}{2\times8\times6}\\\cos\angle OCA&=\frac38.\end{align*}$$
Since $X$ lies on $OC$ and $AX\perp OC$,
$$\begin{align*}CX&=6\cos\angle OCA\\CX&=\frac94\text{ cm}\\OX&=8-\frac94\\OX&=\frac{23}{4}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
The right triangles $OXA$ and $OXB$ have equal hypotenuses and share $OX$, so $XA=XB$. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}XA^2&=8^2-\left(\frac{23}{4}\right)^2\\XA^2&=\frac{495}{16}\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
Apply the cosine rule in $\triangle AXB$:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle AXB&=\frac{XA^2+XB^2-AB^2}{2(XA)(XB)}\\\cos\angle AXB&=\frac{2\left(\frac{495}{16}\right)-36}{2\left(\frac{495}{16}\right)}\\\cos\angle AXB&=\frac{23}{55}\\\angle AXB&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{23}{55}\right)\\\angle AXB&\approx65.28^\circ.\end{align*}$$
